properties.name: McKeldin Library
properties.description: McKeldin Library is the main library on campus. You can find space to study quietly or work in groups, get help with any phase of your research project, and borrow laptops or textbooks. It offers Late Night Study program.

properties.name: Severn Library
properties.description: Severn Library is UMD Libraries’ high-density shelving facility, ten-minutes away from campus on Greenbelt Road. This facility houses unique, semi-rare, and important research collections. All items housed in the Severn Library may be requested through the catalog by anyone with borrowing privileges. Severn Library is a closed-stacks facility, and not accessible to the general public.

properties.name: STEM Library
properties.description: Located in the Mathematics Building, the Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics Library (STEM Library) provides resources and research support to students in engineering, computer, mathematical, and physical sciences disciplines. The STEM Library is also a U.S. Patent and Trademark Resource Center.

properties.name: Architecture Library
properties.description: The Architecture Library is Mondays through Thursdays, from 11:00 AM to 4:00 PM. All students enrolled in programs within the School of Architecture, Planning and Preservation have 24/7 swipe access with their ID cards.

properties.name: Hornbake Library
properties.description: Hornbake Library is home of many unique collections and services at the University of Maryland Libraries, including The Special Collections and University Archives, MITH, Exhibit Gallery, Katherine Anne Porter Room. This library also offers a variety of study spaces available throughout Hornbake Library.

properties.name: Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library
properties.description: The Michelle Smith Performing Arts Library (MSPAL) is the central location on the College Park campus for music, theatre, and dance materials. The circulating, reference, serial, and special collections include 56,000 books, 156,000 musical scores, 130,000 audio and video recordings, 4500 microform titles, and 281 active journal subscriptions.

properties.name: Art Library
properties.description: The Art Library houses more than 100,000 volumes in the areas of art history, archaeology, decorative arts and studio arts, including photography and graphic design. In addition to the print monograph and journal collection, the Library also provides access to a wide variety of art-related electronic resources.

properties.name: Terrapin Tech — McKeldin Library
properties.description: Shop for the latest Apple and Dell products and take advantage of exclusive educational discounts. From computers and tablets to accessories, our staff will work with you to find the technology that best suits your needs. We also offer extended service plans and extra benefits for customers, like on-campus support and loaner laptops to use when a computer needs to be repaired. Select models are displayed in-store, stop by to check them out! Shop Online!\nCertified techs are on hand to assist you with your computer problems. Our experts can assist you with software installations, data backups, virus removals, and more. Terrapin Tech is also an authorized service provider for Apple and Dell and can perform warranty repairs for those products. Terrapin Tech's services are only available to current faculty, staff, students, and affiliates of the University of Maryland, College Park. We are unable to offer support to other visitors.\nDownload software through TERPware. Many packages are available at no cost for the University of Maryland, College Park students, faculty, and staff. Popular products like Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Cloud, and more are available for institutional, work-at-home, and personal use. Do it yourself online or let our technicians assist you with installing and configuring your software.

properties.name: Eppley Recreation Center
properties.description: Named in honor of former varsity athlete, track coach and assistant professor of agronomy Geary "Swede" Eppley, the ERC houses indoor and outdoor swimming pools, fitness machines, squash courts, a running track and an outdoor climbing wall and ropes course.

properties.name: Unity Center
properties.description:
The Unity Center is a student space, grounded in the collective voices of our student body and created to honor and celebrate the richness of our entire campus community. The Unity Center includes five lounges and a multipurpose room. Each of these spaces is crafted to
reflect the cultures it represents, to educate as well as foster connection and a shared sense of belonging for all Terps.

properties.name: Cambridge Community
properties.description: Home of the College Park Scholars living and learning program, the community houses about 1,500 first-and-second-year participants as well as other students. The community includes five residence halls, a community center and a convenience store.

properties.name: Visitor Center
properties.description: Each year the University of Maryland Visitor Center welcomes more than 40,000 visitors. Exhibits include photos of famous alumni and academic accomplishments and The Maryland Moments wall depicts more than 150 years of UMD history.

properties.name: Rossborough Inn
properties.description: Built between 1804 and 1812, the building along with 428 acres was sold by Charles Benedict Calvert to help found what was then called the Maryland Agricultural College. Today, Terrapin Tours start here for prospective students and their families.

properties.name: M Circle
properties.description: Created in 1976 to mark the U.S bicentennial, this landmark draws long lines of students wanting their photo taken on graduation day.

properties.name: Peace Garden
properties.description: Created in 2003, this quiet spot honors the memory of the Sept. 11, 2001, terrorist attacks. The garden marks the spot where the flowers placed along the ODK fountain during a memorial service the next day were buried.

properties.name: Memorial Chapel
properties.description: Dedicated in  1952, the nondenominational chapel honors members of the university community who lost their lives serving the U.S. in the armed forces. Its steeple is the highest point on campus.

properties.name: McKeldin Mall
properties.description: The Omicron Delta Kappa Fountain, etched with quotes from Franklin Delano Roosevelt and Martin Luther King, Jr., is a highlight of the mall. The sundial is a gift from the Class of 1965.

properties.name: Testudo at McKeldin Mall
properties.description: Rubbing the nose on this bronze statue for good luck is one of the university's best-known traditions.

properties.name: Jim Henson Sculpture
properties.description: This life-size homage to the 1960 graduate and Muppets creator shows him sitting with Kermit on a bench outside the Stamp, with just enough room for a visitor to join them.

properties.name: Adele H. Stamp Student Union-Center for Campus Life
properties.description: Stamp attracts nearly 20,000 people a day. The campus information desk, located on the first floor, is a popular resource.

properties.name: Samuel Riggs IV Alumni Center
properties.description: Built by alumni, for alumni, the center is a monument to the achievements of Maryland graduates and a gathering place for friends of the university. The Eric S. & Frann G. Francis Lifetime Member Wall located in the lobby honors life members of the alumni association. The Dessie M. & James R. Moxley Jr. Gardens, facing Byrd Stadium, are an oasis of red, yellow, and white accenting a flowing fountain.

properties.name: Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center
properties.description: The center hosts events in six spaces, from the grand yet inviting 900-seat Dekelboum Concert Hall to the intimate and informal Laboratory Theatre.

properties.name: David C. Driskell Center
properties.description: This modern center honors the legacy of the distinguished university professor, artist, collector and historian. It provides a unique opportunity to study Africa and the African diaspora from multidisciplinary perspectives, particularly the arts, languages, literature and history.

properties.name: Peace Tree
properties.description: In 2009, the university was given this sculpture by artist Han Meilin to commemorate U.S.-Chinese relations. It was installed near the University House.

properties.name: "The Freshman"
properties.description: "The Freshman," located in the Visitor Center, is one of eight Fear the Turtle sculptures on display around campus. Fifty of the sculptures were dedicated by local artists and designers as part of the university's 150th anniversary celebration.

properties.name: The Tree of Life
properties.description: Located in the Garden Chapel, this piece is meant to speak to all faiths. Created in 2013 by artist Catherine Kapikian, woodworker Jim Doman and students, alumni, staff and community volunteers, it is a combination of needlepoint and wood.

properties.name: Parren J. Mitchell Art-Sociology Building
properties.description: The Art Gallery inside puts on five to eight exhibits each year; most are free and open to the public. The gallery is closed between exhibitions and during the summer. In 2010, the Department of Archeology and Art History unveiled the Michelle Smith Collaboratory for Visual Culture featuring a 22-foot-long by 7-foot-high IMAX-like screen.

properties.name: Glenn L. Martin Wind Tunnel
properties.description: This low-speed wind tunnel has been used in aerodynamic research, development and eductaion since 1949, in areas including the design of airplanes, automobiles, sails and submarines.

properties.name: Jeong H. Kim Engineering Building
properties.description: An engineering lab unto itself, the building features exposed columns and beams, a glass-enclosed elevator shaft, two types of bridges and visible color-coded pipes and ducts.

properties.name: Campus Farm
properties.description: This small working farm, which provides hands-on training to students in the animal sciences, includes sheep, cattle, horses and poultry. It harkens back to the university's founding in 1856 as the Maryland Agricultural College.

properties.name: Knight Hall
properties.description: This home for the Philip Merrill College of Journalism, completed in 2010, includes high-tech classrooms, multimedia labs, offices and space for professional journalism centers.

properties.name: Physical Sciences Complex
properties.description: The new 160,000-square-foot building features a multistory elliptical glass cone that opens to the sky and houses the physics and astronomy departments, the Institute for Physical Science and Technology and the Joint Quantum Institute.

properties.name: The Diner
properties.description: One of three campus dining halls, it offers an array of culinary stations to suit many palates and dietary needs.

properties.name: Nyumburu Cultural Center
properties.description: Named for the Swahili word for "freedom house," this is the center for social, cultural and intellectual African-American interaction.

properties.name: Hornbake Library and Plaza
properties.description: Hornbake's highlights include the Katherine Anne Porter Room, established to honor the author's generosity, the National Public Broadcasting Archives, the Library of American Broadcasting and Univeristy Archives. The University Career Center and the President's Promise office are also inside, while the plaza outside is a popular gathering place.

properties.name: South Campus Commons
properties.description: This public-private building partnership provides apartment-style living for 1,825 students, including those in the Beyond the Classroom and Hinman CEOs living and learning programs. The nearby South Campus Dining Hall offers an array of culinary stations to suit many palates, and right above it are the student-run newspaper, The Diamondback, and radio station, WMUC 88.1 FM.

properties.name: South Hill Community / Washington Quad
properties.description: The 14 residence halls known as South Hill are among the oldest on campus; most have been renovated and feature modern apartments and suites. The outdoor area, known as Washington Quad, was recently transformed into a parklike setting where students can relax and socialize.

properties.name: Fraternity Row
properties.description: The site of the first campus football stadium, this area now includes houses for 11 fraternities and three sororities. Today, 22 social fraternities, 15 social sororities, and 18 historically cultural fraternities and sororities are on campus.

properties.name: Cole Student Activities Building
properties.description: The former Cole Field House was home to men's and women's basketball until 2002, and was the site of speeches by Nelson Mandela, Jimmy Carter, Dwight D. Eisenhower and Kofi Annam, performances by Elvis Presley and Bob Hope and NCAA Final Four games. Today it's used for special events and recreation such as indoor soccer and field hockey.

properties.name: Capital One Field at Maryland Stadium
properties.description: In 2012, the university installed a high-tech turf field at the home of Maryland football, designed to keep our athletes cool. A 2009 stadium expansion increased capacity and added skyboxes, a new team store and enhanced seating for fans with disabilities.

properties.name: Gossett Football Team House
properties.description: This all-purpose complex combines football function with imaginative design. Stop in to see the Althetics Hall of Fame displays.

properties.name: Shipley Field at Bob "Turtle" Smith Stadium
properties.description: Named for former baseball and basketball coach H. Burton Shipley and alumnus Bob "Turtle" Smith, it has been home to Maryland baseball since 1965.

properties.name: Xfinity Center
properties.description: Opened in 2002, Xfinity Center is home to Maryland basketball. Stop in to see the 2002 men's and 2006 women's NCAA championship trophies, visit the Terrapin Team Shop or stroll through the Terrapin Walk of Fame and History.

properties.name: Field Hockey and Lacrosse Complex
properties.description: Opened in 2003, this fan-friendly facility is home to the 2011 national champion women's field hockey team and the men's and women's lacrosse teams, both consistent contenders for the NCAA title.

properties.name: University of Maryland Golf Course
properties.description: The 18-hole, championship golf course received a facelift in 2009, enhancing the greens, trees and bunkers, and vital irrigation and drainage systems. The clubhouse features a full-service golf shop. Mulligan's Bar and Grill, locker rooms and banquet facilities.

properties.name: Public Health Garden
properties.description: In the Public Health Garden, students, faculty and staff nurture plants, flowers, vegetables and fruits. Built by students, the garden also serves as a living classroom for agriculture courses.

properties.name: Garden of Reflection and Remembrance
properties.description: In 2010, the university opened the Garden of Reflection and Remembrance on the south side of Memorial Chapel. It's home to native plant and animal species, a landscaped labyrinth, pathways and water elements, designed to encourage quiet thought.

properties.name: Prince Frederick Hall
properties.description: Prince Frederick Hall opened in 2014, housing 462 students. The hall has earned a LEED Gold certification as a "green" building for it's many innovative features, including energy-efficient heating, and cooling systems and elevators that generate electricity on each trip down.

properties.name: Natural Aquatics
properties.description: The indoor and outdoor pools at the Eppley Recreation Center use moss to treat the water. By reducing chemical use, the system provides healthier water for swimmers, and costs less to operate than traditonal water treatment techniques.

properties.name: Marie Mount Hall
properties.description: Marie Mount came to campus in 1919 as the head of the Department of Home and Institution Management and served as the dean of the College of Home Economics from 1927 until her death in 1957. At one time, Miss Mount supposedly lived in the building in a special dean's apartment in the building that bears her name. She was much loved by her students, and University President Wilson Elkins declared in a 1957 memorial to the dean that the character of Marie Mount will live forever. The Maryland Ghosts and Spirits Association detected the presence of numerous spirits in this building during their 2002 visit to campus.

properties.name: Morrill Hall
properties.description: Morrill Hall was named for U. S. Senator Justin S. Morrill of Vermont, the father of the Morrill Land Grant Act of 1862. Originally known as Science Hall, the oldest academic building on the UMD campus has served as classroom and office space for a wide variety of departments since its construction in 1898. The Maryland Ghosts and Spirits Association detected the presence of numerous spirits in this building during their 2002 visit to campus.

properties.name: Tawes Fine Arts Building
properties.description: The Tawes Fine Arts Building, completed in 1965, served as the home for all the performing arts on campus before the 2001 opening of the Clarice Smith Performing Arts Center, and it houses a number of specialized facilities, including a large theater. Over the years, within the walls of Tawes Theater, students have performed such creepy and disturbing plays as "Dracula," "Frankenstein," "The Crucible," and of course the most notorious of haunted and ill-fated plays, "Macbeth."

properties.name: Washington Hall
properties.description: The Washington Hall dormitory was constructed in 1940 and is named for Washington County, Maryland.

properties.name: Easton Hall
properties.description: Easton Hall is named for the county seat of Talbot County, Maryland, and was constructed in 1965.

properties.name: Stamp Student Union
properties.description: Named for the university's first Dean of Women, Adele Hagner Stamp, the Stamp Student Union originally opened in 1955. The Union serves over 16,000 visitors per day and is home to many specialized facilities that serve the campus community, the bookstore, a bank branch, bowling alley, movie theater, food court, mailboxes, large meeting rooms, and the offices for numerous student organizations.

properties.name: H.J. Patterson Hall
properties.description: Constructed in 1931 and named for Harry Jacob Patterson, director of the Maryland Agricultural Experiment Station from 1898 to 1937 and president of the university from 1913 to 1917, H.J. Patterson Hall was originally used for classes in engineering, arts and sciences, agronomy, botany, and physics. At present, it is home to the Departments of Natural Resources Sciences and Cell Biology and Molecular Genetics and a soil testing lab.

properties.name: Alpha Omicron Pi Sorority House
properties.description: The university has a long tradition of Greek Life. The oldest fraternity on campus is Sigma Nu which was established as Gamma Pi in 1913. The first sorority on campus was Kappa Kappa Gamma, originally known as Sigma Delta, established in 1920. Many of the university's fraternity and sorority houses are located on Fraternity Row. Other houses can be found along College Avenue in College Park.

properties.name: Kappa Delta Sorority House
properties.description: The university has a long tradition of Greek Life. The oldest fraternity on campus is Sigma Nu which was established as Gamma Pi in 1913. The first sorority on campus was Kappa Kappa Gamma, originally known as Sigma Delta, established in 1920. Many of the university's fraternity and sorority houses are located on Fraternity Row. Other houses can be found along College Avenue in College Park.

properties.name: McNamee Cemetery
properties.description: The cemetery contains the remains of several members of the McNamee family, who sold the land surrounding this plot to the university in 1938.
